We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction to synthesize target: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. This is a stilbene-like molecule with two anisole (methoxy phenyl) groups attached to a central alkene (trans? but not needed). The hint: Peterson Reaction forms alkenes from alpha-silyl carbanions, breaking C-O (alcohol) and Si-C, forming C=C. So retrosynthesis: target alkene could come from a beta-hydroxy silane precursor: something like C(OH)(SiMe3) attached to phenyl groups? The forward reaction: beta-hydroxy silane -> elimination -> alkene + Si-O? Actually Peterson: alpha-silyl carbanion adds to carbonyl (ketone) to give beta-hydroxy silane, then elimination (acidic or basic) gives alkene, losing Si-O bond and OH as water? The functional groups broken: ketone and trimethylsilyl; formed: C-C double bond. So retrosynthetic step: target alkene derived from a ketone precursor where the carbonyl carbon is attached to one phenyl group and the other side is the other phenyl? Actually the target is symmetrical: central carbon double bond between two carbons each attached to phenyl-OMe groups. So the precursor could be a ketone: (Ar-OMe)C(=O)C(Ar-OMe). That's a diaryl ketone (bis-anisyl ketone). Then apply Peterson: need a trimethylsilyl group attached to carbon adjacent to carbonyl? Wait typical Peterson: R2C=SiMe3 + carbonyl -> beta-hydroxy silane R2C(SiMe3)-C(OH)-R' then elimination to alkene R2C=CR'. So the silane is on one side of the double bond. In our target, both sides are phenyl-OMe groups, no Si. So the precursor could be a ketone where one side is phenyl-OMe, the other side is also phenyl-OMe, and we need a silyl group attached to one side of the carbonyl? Actually the silane is attached to the carbon that becomes one side of the alkene. So the precursor would be a silyl-substituted carbonyl: e.g., (Ar-OMe)C(=O)C(SiMe3)H? Wait the silane is attached to the carbon that will become the alkene carbon after elimination. In Peterson, you start with a silyl carbanion (R3Si-CH2-) which adds to carbonyl to give beta-hydroxy silane: R3Si-CH2-C(OH)-R'. Then elimination yields alkene R3Si-CH=R' after removal of Si-O? Actually the Si remains attached to the carbon of the alkene? No, the elimination removes the Si as a leaving group, forming Si-O bond with the OH, giving alkene R-CH=R' and Si-OH (siloxane). So the final alkene does not have Si. So the precursor is a beta-hydroxy silane: R3Si-CH2-C(OH)-R'. That is formed from addition of silyl carbanion to carbonyl. So retrosynthesis: target alkene -> beta-hydroxy silane precursor (with SiMe3 attached to one carbon, OH on adjacent carbon). Then that beta-hydroxy silane came from a carbonyl (ketone) and a silyl carbanion (trimethylsilyl carbanion). But we only need one reaction step in the route, per task. So we can propose the retrosynthetic step directly from target alkene to a beta-hydroxy silane (the immediate precursor). That is one reaction (the reverse of Peterson elimination). So we need a template ID for Peterson Reaction (reverse). We need to search for template that breaks C-C double bond and forms carbonyl and trimethylsilyl? Actually forward Peterson forms alkene from beta-hydroxy silane, breaking C-O and Si-C, forming C=C. So reverse (retrosynthetic) would break C=C and form C-O and Si-C. So we need a template where functional_groups_broken includes C-C double bond, functional_groups_formed includes ketone and trimethylsilyl? The forward reaction: broken: ketone, trimethylsilyl; formed: C-C double bond. So reverse: broken: C-C double bond; formed: ketone, trimethylsilyl. So we can search with functional_groups_broken ["C-C double bonds"], functional_groups_formed ["ketones","trimethylsilyl"].
